dimensions.explanation: The proposed control concerns a distributor’s offer to a client connected with promoting a specific product or product type. This proposal stays within the circular’s SFC-authorised-fund context. Neither online distribution nor a public campaign is an express prerequisite. The quoted Code language refers more broadly to investment products, but its full actor and product applicability is not supplied.

Distributors are intermediaries distributing the funds. Gifts are not exhaustively defined. Guaranteed returns and other incentives may qualify, rather than qualifying automatically. Product types expressly include certain fund types and funds from certain fund houses. The boundary between a fee discount and a separate cash incentive remains unresolved.

The fee-or-charge discount parenthesis attaches to gifts. It supplies no general exemption from advertising, redemption or statutory requirements. Section 103 authorisation and exemptions attach to the separate statutory invitation control.

The selected rule says distributors 'should not' offer gifts and describes linked gifts as bound by the requirement. The proposed Boolean flags conduct falling within that stated prohibition; it does not label it a section 103 offence. 'May be considered a gift' preserves judgment about classification. Actual investor distraction is expressed as a rationale, not a separate factual prerequisite.

No commencement, expiry or transition rule for the selected control is supplied. The FAQ issue date, 2010-09-30, is reference metadata and cannot be used as the control’s effective date. Temporal applicability must therefore be established separately.

The selected control depends on paragraph 3.11 and the cited FAQ answer. Their complete text and applicable versions are absent. Structured-product classification and section 103 operate separately: a negative structured-product conclusion does not dispose of the gift question. Other Code, handbook and advertising references concern additional controls.

questions: Does the applicable paragraph 3.11 or cited FAQ distinguish direct fee reductions, fee reimbursements and cash rebates, and whose fees or charges qualify?
What establishes the necessary promotional connection for a platform-wide or mixed-product campaign, including a campaign limited to one fund house?
Which version and effective period of paragraph 3.11 and FAQ answer 1 govern the assessed offer, and have later materials changed their application?
What additional applicability provisions determine the control’s reach beyond the circular’s SFC-authorised-fund distributors?

assumptions: Assess one identified benefit offered in one identified promotion; a mixed package requires separate classification of its components.
The proposal is limited to SFC-authorised-fund distribution and assumes temporal applicability has been established separately.
Gift status, discount status and promotional linkage remain supplied judgments; no unknown fact is assigned a truth value.
The packet supports one definite core reading. The treatment of rebates and indirect promotional links remains unresolved rather than being converted into unsupported competing rules.

citations.quote: as they may be considered a gift that should not be offered to investors.

Paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct provides that distributors should not offer any gifts (other than a discount of fees or charges) in promoting a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product to a client.

If gifts are offered in such a way that they are linked to a particular type of investment product, such as certain types of funds or funds offered by certain fund houses, then such gifts will be bound by this requirement
in breach of section 103 of the SFO or paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct.
3 The answer to question 1 of the frequently asked questions on the Code of Conduct issued by the SFC on 30 September 2010.

readings.distinction: The selected control turns on a non-exempt gift offered in a product-linked promotion. It is not an unconditional ban on every additional return, and it does not require either structured-product status or proof of actual distraction. Its strongest unresolved boundary is whether a particular monetary benefit genuinely constitutes a fee or charge discount; the supplied text does not settle rebate mechanics.

readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_PROHIBITED] For the selected paragraph-10 gift-promotion control, within the stated scope, true means the offered benefit is a gift falling outside the fee-or-charge discount exception and thus falls within the stated 'should not offer' requirement. False means only that this selected gift condition is not met; an out-of-scope offer is not assessed. Neither outcome establishes overall compliance or resolves section 103.
